title: Which Online Marketplace for Farmers in the Philippines Is Best for Selling Produce?
metaTitle: Online Marketplace for Farmers: Where to Sell in the PH
metaDescription: No single online marketplace for farmers fits every crop. Compare Kadiwa, NFA, DA buyer matching and online selling, and keep buyers and prices on record.
excerpt: There is no single best online marketplace for farmers in the Philippines. Most farmers sell best through a mix: DA Kadiwa outlets and buyer matching, NFA buying stations for palay, a cooperative, and online selling to buyers they can deliver to. anee.io, a farm app built for Filipino farmers, is not a marketplace and does not buy or sell produce, but it keeps your harvest records, buyers and prices so you sell from real numbers.

blocks.text:
Selling is where many seasons are won or lost. You can grow a good crop and still earn little if you sell wet palay to the first trader, or if your tomatoes ripen the week the market is full.

An app alone will not fix that. But the right channels, a clear price floor and good records will. Here is what works today, and what to check before you trust any platform.

items: Government channels such as Kadiwa stores and DA buyer matching usually work through registered farmer groups.
The NFA buys palay from farmers listed in the RSBSA, at its buying stations, with moisture and purity standards.
Online selling through social media, chat apps or marketplace sites suits buyers you can reach and deliver to.
anee.io does not buy produce, sell inputs or take payments. It keeps your records, contacts and community in one place.

blocks.text: What should an online marketplace for farmers offer?
Before you list a harvest on any site or group, ask the same questions you would ask a trader at the farm gate. If a platform cannot answer them, sell somewhere else.

blocks.text: Kadiwa, DA buyer matching and the NFA

The Kadiwa program lets farmers and producers sell fresh and processed products directly to consumers, without middlemen. Associations in the program must be duly registered and compliant with all requirements. In the same way, the DA Agribusiness and Marketing Assistance Service links farmers' groups with consumer markets and institutional buyers. So a [Filipino farmer community](/blog/filipino-farmer-community-online) that is a registered cooperative opens doors a single farmer cannot.

For palay, the NFA is a price floor worth knowing. In Nueva Ecija in 2020, the NFA bought only from legitimate farmers listed in the RSBSA or members of farmers' organizations. It also asked for palay at 14 percent moisture or less and at least 96 percent purity. Check today's buying price at your NFA branch, and compare it with the [palay price](/blog/palay-price-philippines) traders offer.

blocks.title: Dry it before you sell it
blocks.text: Wet palay sells for less, and buyers often deduct for moisture. If you can dry to the NFA standard before you sell, you can choose between buyers instead of taking the first offer. Note the moisture of every load, because it explains the price you got.
How do you sell produce online safely?

items.title: Know your floor price
items.text: Add up what the crop cost you per kilo before you post a price. Our guide to [farm profitability](/blog/farm-profitability) shows how. Never sell below your cost just to clear a harvest unless the crop will spoil.

items.title: Check market prices
items.text: The DA gathers prices along the value chain of basic crops and publishes them through its market information service. Ask your agriculture office where your region posts them.

items.title: Post clear facts
items.text: Show the crop, the harvest date, the volume, the grade and your pickup point. Use real photos from your field, not stock pictures.

items.title: Agree in writing
items.text: Confirm the price, volume, delivery and payment in one chat message. A screenshot is your record if anything goes wrong.

items.title: Get paid at delivery
items.text: For new buyers, ask for payment on delivery or a partial payment first. Do not release a big load on a promise.

items.title: Record the sale
items.text: Write the buyer, the price, the volume and any rejects the same day. Next season you will know who paid fairly.

blocks.text: Can you buy farm inputs on an online marketplace for farmers?

You can, but check before you pay. Buy fertilizer and pesticides from dealers licensed by the FPA, and check the active ingredient against your problem first. Our guides on [fertilizer brands and dealers](/blog/fertilizer-brands-and-dealers) and on how to [avoid buying the wrong pesticide](/blog/avoid-buying-the-wrong-pesticide) cover what to check. Always follow the product label and its FPA registration.
How does anee.io help you sell if it is not a marketplace?
anee.io does not buy your harvest, sell you inputs or handle payments for produce. Its Shop is marked coming soon and is not open. What it does is keep the facts that make you a better seller.

items: **[Harvest records](/features/harvest-records)**: after harvest, note the yield and moisture per lot, the buyer and the price, and any problems. Next season you plan from real numbers.
**Contact List**: keep buyers, traders and haulers with notes and tags such as Buyer, so you find them in seconds every season.
**Profit Report**: your sales from the harvest records against everything the season cost, on paid plans.
**Compare Reports**: two seasons side by side, and Anee explains what changed, using credits.
**The community**: ask other growers where they sell and what buyers paid this week.

blocks.text: Questions about selling farm produce online

items.q: What is the best online marketplace for farmers in the Philippines?
items.a: No single platform is best for every crop. Palay often sells best to the NFA, a miller or a trusted trader, while vegetables and fruit can sell direct online or through Kadiwa. Most farmers do best with two or three channels and good records.

items.q: Does anee.io buy or sell farm products?
items.a: No. anee.io is a farm app, not a marketplace. It does not buy produce, sell inputs or take payments for produce. It helps you keep harvest records, buyer contacts and prices, and it has a farmer community.

items.q: How can I sell palay to the NFA?
items.a: Register in the RSBSA through your municipal agriculture office, then ask the nearest NFA branch about its buying price and requirements. The NFA has asked for at most 14 percent moisture and at least 96 percent purity.
Kadiwa works with registered farmers' associations and cooperatives that meet DA requirements. Ask your DA regional office or its marketing division what your group needs to qualify.

items.q: How do I avoid scams when I sell online?
items.a: Agree on the price, volume and payment in writing before you deliver. For new buyers, ask for payment on delivery or a partial payment first, and keep screenshots of every deal.
